detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted for filing the NDA for an ALK-selective inhibitor in TKI pre-treated advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer and granted Priority Review. A PDUFA target action date of November 27, 2026 was assigned. This acceptance accelerates the potential review timeline for a therapy aimed at overcoming resistance and CNS involvement.
catalyst_text_evidence: The U.S. FDA has accepted for filing Nuvalent's NDA for neladalkib, an investigational ALK-selective inhibitor, in tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) pre-treated advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The application has been granted Priority Review and assigned a PDUFA target action date of 2026-11-27.

catalyst_text: NDA accepted with PDUFA September 18 2026 assigned
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted for filing the NDA for a ROS1-selective inhibitor for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer who received at least one prior ROS1 TKI. The application was assigned a PDUFA target action date of September 18, 2026. This regulatory milestone advances a potential option for patients with resistant disease and CNS metastases.
catalyst_text_evidence: Based on results for tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) pre-treated patients with advanced ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) enrolled in the global registrational ARROS-1 Phase 1/2 clinical trial, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for filing Nuvalent's NDA submission for zidesamtinib for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC who received at least 1 prior ROS1 TKI. The application has been assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-09-18.

catalyst_text: Submitted NDA for TKI pretreated ALK positive NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: An NDA was submitted to the FDA for neladalkib in TKI pre-treated advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer, based on data from the registrational ALKOVE-1 Phase 1/2 trial. This marks a key regulatory milestone that begins FDA review and could enable potential U.S. approval if the application is accepted and favorably reviewed.
catalyst_text_evidence: CAMBRIDGE, Mass., 2026-04-07 /PRNewswire/ -- Nuvalent, Inc. (NASDAQ:NUVL)... today announced the submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of the Company's NDA for neladalkib, an investigational ALK-selective inhibitor, in TKI pre-treated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC. The application is based on data in TKI pre-treated patients with advanced ALK-positive NSCLC treated with neladalkib in the global, registration-directed ALKOVE-1 Phase 1/2 clinical trial.

catalyst_text: NDA Accepted w/ PDUFA set for September 18, 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted for filing a New Drug Application for zidesamtinib for adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with at least one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor. The acceptance includes assignment of a PDUFA target action date of 2026-09-18, initiating formal regulatory review.
catalyst_text_evidence: Nuvalent, Inc. (NASDAQ:NUVL), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on creating precisely targeted therapies for clinically proven kinase targets in cancer, today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for filing its New Drug Application (NDA) for zidesamtinib, an investigational ROS1-selective inhibitor, for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who received at least 1 prior ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). The application has been assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-09-18.

drug_indication: TKI pre-treated patients with advanced ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
catalyst_text: Announced positive pivotal data from the global ARROS-1 Phase 1/2 trial of zidesamtinib, a novel ROS1-selective inhibitor, in TKI-pretreated patients with advanced ROS1-positive NSCLC.

Further Phase 1 results revealed promising effectiveness and sustainability in patients with ALK-positive NSCLC who had undergone extensive prior treatment, as reported on September 9, 2024. This information is anticipated to be shared at ESMO in September.

Data from Phase 1 showed promising effectiveness and lasting results in individuals with previously treated ROS1-positive NSCLC, as reported on September 9, 2024. This information will be shared at ESMO on September 14, 2024.
The initiation of Phase 1a/1b has been recorded as of July 22, 2024.
